ds.

Aggregated and anonymized cohort reports are considered outside the scope of the GDPR, as they do not contain personal data and cannot be used to identify individual data subjects. These reports are retained indefinitely for historical benchmarking and longitudinal trend analysis purposes.

The DPAs default to NovaBridge\'s standard retention schedule as described above unless the enterprise client requests shorter retention periods in writing. To date, no enterprise client has submitted a request for a shorter retention period.

The automated purge jobs referenced above are managed by the NovaBridge platform engineering team and execute on a weekly cadence, deleting all data records that have exceeded the applicable retention period as of the execution date.

**[5. Cross-Border Data Transfers and ML Model Training]{.underline}**

**5.1 Primary Data Storage**

All EU personal data processed through the PulseView platform --- encompassing all three categories described in Section 2 (survey responses, productivity metrics, and sentiment analysis outputs) --- is stored in the AWS eu-central-1 region located in Frankfurt, Germany. The Frankfurt AWS region was selected as the primary storage location for EU personal data in order to ensure compliance with data localization expectations, minimize cross-border transfer risk, and provide low-latency access for EU-based operations.

No EU personal data is stored at rest in any non-EU/EEA location for the primary processing purposes of survey administration, productivity metric reporting, or sentiment analysis output delivery to enterprise clients. All client-facing processing, reporting, and data delivery activities are performed entirely within the Frankfurt environment.

**5.2 Transfer to Austin for ML Model Training**

Notwithstanding the primary EU storage arrangement described above, NovaBridge transfers **pseudonymized** EU personal data from the Frankfurt AWS environment to NovaBridge Technologies, Inc.\'s infrastructure located in Austin, Texas for the purpose of **global ML model training and improvement**.

**Pseudonymization.** In this context, \"pseudonymized\" means that direct identifiers --- including employee names, email addresses, and other attributes that could be used to directly identify an individual --- are replaced with tokenized pseudonymous identifiers prior to transfer. The pseudonymization process is performed within the Frankfurt environment before any data leaves the EU/EEA. However, the pseudonymization is **reversible** by NovaBridge Technologies EU B.V., which retains the re-identification mapping table in the Frankfurt environment. NovaBridge Technologies, Inc. (the Austin-based entity) does not have access to the re-identification key or the mapping table. From the perspective of the Austin data science teams, the data received consists of pseudonymous identifiers associated with survey response data, productivity metric data, and sentiment analysis scores, without the ability to link these records to identified individuals.

**Model Training Purpose.** NovaBridge US data science teams use the pseudonymized EU data, combined with data from other global regions, to train, validate, and improve the machine learning models that power PulseView\'s sentiment analysis, burnout risk, and flight risk features. Model training is an iterative process in which historical data is used to refine model parameters, test model accuracy against known outcomes, and develop new model features. Model improvements resulting from training activities are deployed globally across all PulseView instances, including the EU production environment.

**Purpose Limitation in DPAs.** This transfer for model training purposes is **not described as a separate processing purpose** in the DPAs executed with enterprise clients. The DPAs describe the overall processing purpose as \"provision of workforce analytics services\" and do not carve out model training, model improvement, or product development as a distinct processing activity. NovaBridge treats model training as an incidental and ancillary activity within the broader scope of the primary processing purpose --- namely, the delivery and continuous improvement of the PulseView platform.

**Privacy Notice Disclosures.** The privacy notices provided to data subjects through the consent pop-up (described in Section 3) state that \"data may be processed in jurisdictions outside the EU/EEA for service improvement purposes.\" The privacy notices do not specifically identify ML model training as a separate processing purpose, do not describe the nature or scope of model training activities, and do not identify NovaBridge Technologies, Inc. by name as the recipient of transferred data for this purpose.

**Transfer Mechanism.** The cross-border transfer of pseudonymized EU personal data to NovaBridge Technologies, Inc. in Austin is governed by **Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)**, utilizing the European Commission\'s June 4, 2021 version. The SCCs are executed as **Module 3 (processor-to-processor)**, with NovaBridge Technologies EU B.V. as the data exporter (in its capacity as processor) and NovaBridge Technologies, Inc. as the data importer (in its capacity as sub-processor).

**Supplementary Measures.** In addition to the SCCs, NovaBridge has implemented the following supplementary technical and organizational measures for data in transit and at rest in the Austin environment: encryption in transit using TLS 1.3 for all data transfers between Frankfurt and Austin; encryption at rest using AES-256 for all stored data in the Austin environment; and role-based access controls limiting Austin-based personnel to pseudonymized datasets, with access restricted to members of the data science and model engineering teams who have completed GDPR awareness training.

**5.3 Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA)**

A Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) was completed in **March 2023** to evaluate the legal and practical risks associated with the transfer of EU personal data to the United States. The TIA was prepared by Tomás Herrera-Vidal, CPO/DPO, with substantive input and review by outside counsel Margaux Leclerc of Valcourt Deschênes LLP.

The TIA assessed the general legal framework in the United States as it pertains to NovaBridge\'s data transfers, with particular consideration given to: U.S. foreign intelligence surveillance laws, including Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) and Executive Order 12333; the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF) and the European Commission\'s associated adequacy decision adopted in July 2023; and the supplementary technical and organizational measures implemented by NovaBridge (described in Section 5.2 above).

The TIA is a **general-purpose assessment** covering all EU-to-US data transfers conducted by NovaBridge, including both primary processing support activities (such as L2 technical support access from Austin-based support engineers) and the model training transfers described in Section 5.2. The TIA does **not** contain a separate, purpose-specific analysis dedicated to the model-training transfer. It does not separately assess the risks particular to model-training processing, the volume and sensitivity of data transferred specifically for model training, or the specific personnel access controls and data handling procedures applicable to the model-training use case as distinct from general support access.

The TIA has not been updated since its completion in March 2023 --- approximately 22 months as of the date of this memorandum. No interim review has been conducted to assess whether the TIA\'s conclusions remain valid in light of subsequent regulatory, legal, or operational developments.

NovaBridge is aware of the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF) adequacy decision adopted by the European Commission on July 10, 2023. However, NovaBridge Technologies, Inc. has not yet completed the self-certification process under the DPF with the U.S. Department of Commerce. Accordingly, NovaBridge does not currently rely on the DPF adequacy decision as a transfer mechanism and continues to rely solely on the SCCs described in Section 5.2.

**[6. Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) Status]{.underline}**

**Original DPIA.** A Data Protection Impact Assessment was completed in **June 2022**, prior to the launch of the PulseView platform\'s EU operations. The original DPIA covered the following processing activities:

> • Collection and processing of employee survey responses (Category 1);
>
> • Collection and processing of productivity metrics (Category 2);
>
> • Cross-border transfer of pseudonymized data to NovaBridge Technologies, Inc. in Austin, Texas; and
>
> • General data security and access control measures.

The original DPIA identified the processing as likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, given the scale of processing (at the time, approximately 2.5 million data subjects, subsequently grown to 3.2 million), the nature of the data processed (workforce productivity and engagement data in an employment context), and the inherent power imbalance between employers and employees. The DPIA concluded that the implemented safeguards --- including pseudonymization, aggregated reporting, access controls, and the SCCs for cross-border transfers --- were sufficient to mitigate the identified risks to an acceptable level.

**September 2023 Update.** The DPIA was updated in **September 2023** to incorporate the sentiment analysis module launched in Q3 2023. This update:

> • Described the machine learning model inputs (survey responses and productivity metrics) and outputs (sentiment scores, burnout risk indicators, and flight risk predictions);
>
> • Assessed the sentiment analysis feature as an additional processing activity layered on top of the existing survey and productivity metric processing;
>
> • Documented the consent-based legal basis (Article 6(1)(a)) for sentiment analysis processing;
>
> • Reviewed the aggregated cohort delivery model as the mechanism by which sentiment analysis results are shared with enterprise clients.

However, the September 2023 DPIA update contains the following noted limitations:

> • The update **did not** specifically analyze whether the generation of per-employee sentiment scores, burnout risk indicators, and flight risk predictions constitutes **profiling** within the meaning of Article 4(4) GDPR, or whether such processing triggers the protections and obligations of **Article 22 GDPR** (automated individual decision-making, including profiling). The update treated the aggregated cohort delivery model --- whereby individual scores are never directly shared with the enterprise client --- as sufficient mitigation, without conducting a separate analysis of the per-employee score generation and retention step itself.
>
> • The update **did not** analyze the transfer of data to Austin for ML model training as a **separate processing purpose**. Model training was addressed only as part of the general \"service provision\" purpose and was not subject to a distinct risk assessment.
>
> • The update **did not** incorporate or reference any regulatory guidance post-dating September 2023, including the EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 on the processing of personal data in the context of workplace monitoring technologies (adopted December 12, 2024) or the AP enforcement decision No. AP-2025-0042 against TalentScope B.V. (published January 15, 2025).

The DPIA has not been reviewed or updated since September 2023 --- a period of approximately 16 months as of the date of this memorandum.

NovaBridge EU, as a processor, is aware that Article 35(11) GDPR requires data controllers to carry out a review of DPIAs at least when there is a change in the risk represented by processing operations. While this obligation rests primarily on the controller, NovaBridge EU recognizes its role in supporting controllers\' compliance and has not yet assessed whether recent regulatory developments --- including the EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 and the AP Decision No. AP-2025-0042 --- constitute a triggering change that would warrant a comprehensive DPIA refresh, either by NovaBridge on its own initiative or in coordination with its enterprise clients.

No consultation with the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens or any other supervisory authority under Article 36 GDPR has been sought in connection with the PulseView processing activities.

**[7. Compliance Monitoring and Risk Register Summary]{.underline}**

NovaBridge Technologies EU B.V. maintains a GDPR compliance tracker in the form of a structured spreadsheet, updated periodically by the CPO/DPO office. The tracker catalogs all key compliance obligations, the relevant GDPR provisions, the current compliance status rating, and the date of the most recent assessment for each item.

The table below summarizes the current compliance status ratings as reflected in the most recent review cycle:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Compliance Item**                      **Relevant Provision**            **Status**        **Last Assessed**
  ---------------------------------------- --------------------------------- ----------------- -------------------
  DPO appointment                          Article 37 GDPR                   **Compliant**     January 2025

  DPAs with EU clients                     Article 28 GDPR                   **Compliant**     November 2024

  Legal bases documented                   Article 6 GDPR                    **Compliant**     September 2023

  Data Protection Impact Assessment        Article 35 GDPR                   **Compliant**     September 2023

  Transfer Impact Assessment               Articles 44--49, *Schrems II*     **Compliant**     March 2023

  Standard Contractual Clauses             Articles 46(2)(c) GDPR            **Compliant**     March 2023

  Data retention policy                    Article 5(1)(e) GDPR              **Compliant**     August 2023

  Consent mechanism (sentiment analysis)   Article 6(1)(a), Article 7 GDPR   **Compliant**     September 2023

  EU data storage location (primary)       Data localization best practice   **Compliant**     January 2025
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

These ratings reflect the compliance team\'s assessment as of the date indicated in the \"Last Assessed\" column for each item. Notably, the ratings for legal bases, DPIA, TIA, SCCs, data retention, and consent mechanism **have not yet been updated** to account for the EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 on the processing of personal data in the context of workplace monitoring technologies (adopted December 12, 2024) or the AP Decision No. AP-2025-0042 against TalentScope B.V. (published January 15, 2025).

A comprehensive review of these compliance ratings in light of the new regulatory developments is pending. This review will be initiated upon receipt of outside counsel\'s preliminary analysis from Valcourt Deschênes LLP, which has been requested and is expected by the end of January 2025. Upon completion of outside counsel\'s analysis, the CPO/DPO office will conduct a full re-assessment of each compliance item and update the tracker accordingly, with findings to be reported to Aisling Brennan, Deputy General Counsel, and to the NovaBridge EU board of directors.

**[8. Key Contacts and Responsibilities]{.underline}**

The following table identifies the key personnel and external advisors responsible for NovaBridge\'s GDPR compliance program in connection with the PulseView platform:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Name**              **Role**                    **Entity**                        **Email**                        **Responsibility**
  --------------------- --------------------------- --------------------------------- -------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Tomás Herrera-Vidal   CPO / DPO                   NovaBridge Technologies EU B.V.   therrera@novabridge.eu           GDPR compliance oversight, DPIA management, DPO functions under Article 37--39, supervisory authority liaison, privacy-by-design review

  Aisling Brennan       Deputy General Counsel      NovaBridge Technologies, Inc.     abrennan@novabridge.com          Privacy legal strategy, DPA negotiations and template management, regulatory risk assessment, coordination with outside counsel

  Raina Chaudhary       VP of Engineering           NovaBridge Technologies, Inc.     rchaudhary@novabridge.com        Platform architecture, data pipeline management, privacy-by-design implementation, consent flow technical design, data retention automation

  Margaux Leclerc       Partner (Outside Counsel)   Valcourt Deschênes LLP            m.leclerc@valcourtdeschenes.eu   EU regulatory advice, enforcement defense strategy, EDPB guidance interpretation, supervisory authority engagement
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In addition to the individuals listed above, NovaBridge\'s securities counsel, **Kessler Whitmore LLP** (350 Park Avenue, 28th Floor, New York, NY 10022), is handling the preparation of the company\'s IPO S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Kessler Whitmore has flagged GDPR compliance as a disclosure priority within the S-1 risk factors and has requested that the Privacy & Compliance team provide a current compliance summary and risk assessment for inclusion in the registration statement\'s risk factor disclosures.

NovaBridge\'s cyber and privacy liability insurance is underwritten by **Albion Specialty Insurance Ltd.**, under a policy that includes coverage for regulatory defense costs and data protection authority fines where legally insurable. The policy includes a GDPR fine sub-limit of **€5,000,000**. All material regulatory inquiries, supervisory authority correspondence, and enforcement-related developments must be promptly reported to Albion Specialty in accordance with the policy\'s notice provisions.

**[9. Document Version History]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Version**       **Date**           **Author**            **Changes**
  ----------------- ------------------ --------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1.0               May 2022           Tomás Herrera-Vidal   Initial document covering employee survey response processing and productivity metric processing; cross-border transfer framework described; DPA and DPIA status documented.

  2.0               August 2023        Tomás Herrera-Vidal   Added sentiment analysis module description (Category 3); documented consent mechanism design and implementation; updated retention schedule to include sentiment analysis outputs; expanded Section 5 on cross-border transfers.

  3.0               September 2023     Tomás Herrera-Vidal   Aligned with September 2023 DPIA update; added TIA reference (March 2023); updated compliance tracker ratings; editorial corrections throughout.

  3.1               January 10, 2025   Tomás Herrera-Vidal   Minor updates to data subject volume (3.2M), client count (740+), and revenue figures for FY 2024. No substantive changes to processing descriptions, legal bases, or compliance assessments.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Note:** Version 3.1 is a factual refresh only, updating key operational metrics to reflect current figures. A substantive review of this document in light of the EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 (adopted December 12, 2024) and the AP Decision No. AP-2025-0042 (published January 15, 2025) is pending and will be conducted as part of the broader compliance review described in Section 7.

*End of Document*

This memorandum is classified as Confidential --- Internal Use Only. Distribution is limited to the individuals identified on the cover page. This document is not intended to constitute legal advice and should not be relied upon as such. For legal analysis of the matters described herein, consult outside counsel at Valcourt Deschênes LLP.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor, Inches, Cm
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document()
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.9)
sec.top_margin = sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.8)
st = doc.styles["Normal"]; st.font.name = "Calibri"; st.font.size = Pt(10.5)
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
for lvl, sz in ((1, 14), (2, 12), (3, 11)):
    h = doc.styles["Heading %d" % lvl]; h.font.name = "Calibri"; h.font.size = Pt(sz)
    h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)

NAVY = "1F3A5F"
RAG = {"RED": "F4CCCC", "AMBER": "FCE5CD", "GREEN": "D9EAD3", "HDR": "1F3A5F", "GREY": "EEEEEE"}

def shade(cell, color):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    s = OxmlElement("w:shd"); s.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); s.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); s.set(qn("w:fill"), color)
    tcPr.append(s)

def add_runs(p, text):
    # **bold** markup
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, t in enumerate(parts):
        if t:
            r = p.add_run(t); r.bold = (i % 2 == 1)
    return p

def para(text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None, align=None, space_after=6):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text)
    for r in p.runs:
        if bold: r.bold = True
        if italic: r.italic = True
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if align: p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

def bullet(text, level=0, style="List Bullet"):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style if level == 0 else style + " 2")
    add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def num(text):
    return bullet(text, style="List Number")

def table(headers, rows, widths=None, rag_col=None, font=9):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""
        r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        shade(c, RAG["HDR"])
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, str(v))
            for r in p.runs: r.font.size = Pt(font)
            if rag_col is not None and i == rag_col:
                key = str(v).split()[0].strip("*").upper()
                if key in RAG: shade(cells[i], RAG[key])
    # repeat header
    trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true"); trPr.append(th)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def callout(text, color="FFF2CC"):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1); t.style = "Table Grid"
    c = t.rows[0].cells[0]; c.text = ""; shade(c, color)
    lines = text.split("\n")
    p = c.paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, lines[0])
    for ln in lines[1:]:
        p = c.add_paragraph(); add_runs(p, ln)
    for p in c.paragraphs:
        for r in p.runs: r.font.size = Pt(10)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

# footer
fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
fp.text = "Privileged & Confidential - Prepared at the direction of counsel - Attorney-Client Communication / Attorney Work Product - Do not forward"
fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
for r in fp.runs: r.font.size = Pt(8); r.italic = True

# ---------------- Title block
para("PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT", bold=True, size=9, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
para("Prepared at the direction of the Deputy General Counsel for the purpose of obtaining and acting on legal advice. Limited distribution - do not forward, excerpt, or paste into the S-1 or other external materials without Legal sign-off.", italic=True, size=8.5, align=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
r = p.add_run("EXECUTIVE REGULATORY BRIEF"); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(18); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
r = p.add_run("New EU Rules on Workforce Analytics: What the EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 and the Dutch TalentScope Fine Mean for PulseView"); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(12)

callout(
"**In one sentence:** EU regulators have just said, in guidance (December 2024) and in a EUR 8.5 million fine against a near-identical competitor (January 2025), that the way PulseView currently collects, scores, keeps and moves employee data is not lawful - and our own regulator, the Dutch AP, is the one that issued the fine.\n"
"**1. This is current law, not a future rule.** The Dutch AP applied the EDPB guidance to conduct that pre-dated it and said companies cannot claim a grace period. Every gap below is a present-day exposure.\n"
"**2. PulseView matches all four grounds of the TalentScope fine** - legal basis for productivity tracking, missing DPIA coverage of per-employee scoring, over-long data retention, and no purpose-specific transfer assessment for US model training - and has additional gaps TalentScope was not even fined for (our consent flow fails every element of the new consent test).\n"
"**3. Our compliance tracker is materially out of date.** It rates every item Green / Compliant. On the facts in our own documents, at least nine items should be Red or Amber today. We should not hand the current tracker to S-1 counsel, auditors or investors as a status report.\n"
"**4. Realistic fine exposure is roughly EUR 8 million, and the legal ceiling is EUR 20 million - not the EUR 11.6 million in our tracker and in counsel memos.** Our EUR 5 million insurance sub-limit may not pay at all, because GDPR fines may not be insurable in the Netherlands.\n"
"**5. The IPO (Q3 2025) is the forcing deadline.** We have roughly six months to show a credible, documented remediation programme that can be described in the S-1 risk factors. Several fixes need engineering work (consent redesign, per-employee scoring, retention) and contract changes across 740+ client DPAs, so they must start now.", color="E8EEF7")

para("**What we are asking leadership to do now** (detail in Section 8):", space_after=3)
num("Approve a funded GDPR remediation programme with an accountable executive sponsor and weekly status reporting through IPO.")
num("Decide on immediate interim risk-reduction steps for PulseView (Section 7, \"first 30 days\"), including whether to pause or limit EU per-employee scoring and US model-training transfers pending remediation.")
num("Authorise Legal to brief the Board audit committee and Kessler Whitmore (S-1 counsel) on a corrected risk picture, and to engage Albion Specialty on insurance coverage.")

# ---------------- 2. What changed
doc.add_heading("2. What changed - in plain language", level=1)
doc.add_heading("2.1 The new EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 (adopted 12 December 2024)", level=2)
para("The EDPB is the body of all EU data protection regulators. Its guidelines are not legislation, but regulators use them to decide cases, and departing from them requires strong justification. These are the first EU-wide guidelines aimed squarely at AI-driven workforce analytics. Five positions matter to us:")

    ["2", "No DPIA specifically covering predictive scoring (Art. 35)", "A general platform DPIA was not enough; each high-risk feature needs its own analysis, including of per-employee scoring and Art. 22."],
    ["3", "Keeping raw survey and productivity data for 30 months (Art. 5(1)(e))", "The AP said 12 months was enough for analytics; \"more data improves analytics\" is not a justification; model training cannot justify retention without its own legal basis.     ["4", "No purpose-specific TIA for US model-training transfers (Art. 46(1))", "Pseudonymisation alone did not cure it; the general TIA was ~18 months old and never reviewed. The AP also flagged that the SCC module should match the parties' real roles."],
], widths=[0.3, 2.6, 3.8])

def shade(cell, color):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    s = OxmlElement("w:shd"); s.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); s.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); s.set(qn("w:fill"), color)

def add_runs(p, text):
    # **bold** markup
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, t in enumerate(parts):
        if t:
            r = p.add_run(t); r.bold = (i % 2 == 1)
    return p

def para(text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None, align=None, space_after=6):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text)
    for r in p.runs:
        if bold: r.bold = True
        if italic: r.italic = True
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if align: p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

def bullet(text, level=0, style="List Bullet"):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style if level == 0 else style + " 2")
    add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def num(text):
    return bullet(text, style="List Number")

def table(headers, rows, widths=None, rag_col=None, font=9):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""
        r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        shade(c, RAG["HDR"])
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, str(v))
            for r in p.runs: r.font.size = Pt(font)
            if rag_col is not None and i == rag_col:
                key = str(v).split()[0].strip("*").upper()
                if key in RAG: shade(cells[i], RAG[key])
    # repeat header
    trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true"); trPr.append(th)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def callout(text, color="FFF2CC"):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1); t.style = "Table Grid"
    c = t.rows[0].cells[0]; c.text = ""; shade(c, color)
    lines = text.split("\n")
    p = c.paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, lines[0])
    for ln in lines[1:]:
        p = c.add_paragraph(); add_runs(p, ln)
    for p in c.paragraphs:
        for r in p.runs: r.font.size = Pt(10)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

doc.add_heading("2.1 The new EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 (adopted 12 December 2024)", level=2)
para("The EDPB is the body of all EU data protection regulators. Its guidelines are not legislation, but regulators use them to decide cases, and departing from them requires strong justification. These are the first EU-wide guidelines aimed squarely at AI-driven workforce analytics. Five positions matter to us:")
table(["Topic", "What the guidelines now say (plain language)", "Ref."], [
    ["Tracking productivity", "\"Legitimate interest\" - the legal basis our DPAs use - is generally **not** a valid basis for continuous or daily collection of individual productivity data (app usage, meetings, email volume). Employers need a stronger basis such as a works-council / collective agreement, specific national law, or genuinely free consent. Vendors whose standard DPA pre-selects legitimate interest may themselves be liable.", "Para. 34"],
    ["Employee consent", "Consent at work is presumed **not** freely given unless the company can prove all four of: (a) no penalty or loss of access for saying no; (b) separate choices for separate purposes - no single \"I Agree\"; (c) a real alternative way to do the task; (d) withdrawal as easy as giving consent. Acceptance rates above 90-95% are a red flag.", "Para. 47"],
    ["Predictive scores", "Sentiment, burnout and flight-risk scores about individual employees are \"profiling\". The protections for automated decision-making (Art. 22) apply **when the per-employee score is created and stored**, even if clients only ever see aggregated team reports. Safeguards required: meaningful explanation of the logic, a way for employees to get human review and contest a score, and bias/accuracy testing. Regulators prefer designs that never create individual scores.", "Para. 58"],
    ["Training our AI models", "Using client data to train our own models is a **separate purpose** that needs its own legal basis, its own description in DPAs and privacy notices, and its own retention rule. Pseudonymised data is still personal data. A vendor training its own product models may be a **controller** (not just a processor) for that activity.", "Para. 71"],
    ["Sending data to the US for training", "Each transfer purpose needs its own risk assessment. ], widths=[1.2, 4.8, 0.7])

def add_runs(p, text):
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, t in enumerate(parts):
        if t:

    return p

def para(text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None, align=None, space_after=6):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()

    for r in p.runs:
        if bold: r.bold = True
        if italic: r.italic = True
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

    t = doc.add_table(rows=1 if header else 0, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER

        trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true"); trPr.append(th)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, str(v))
            for r in p.runs: r.font.size = Pt(font)
            if rag_col is not None and i == rag_col:
                key = str(v).split()[0].strip("*").upper() if str(v).strip() else ""
                if key in RAG: shade(cells[i], RAG[key])
    if widths:

            for i, w in enumerate(widths):

    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

doc.add_heading("2. What changed – in plain language", level=1)
doc.add_heading("2.1 EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 (adopted 12 December 2024)", level=2)
para("The EDPB is the body of all EU data protection regulators. Its guidelines are not legislation, but regulators use them to decide cases, and departing from them requires strong justification. These are the first EU-wide guidelines aimed squarely at AI-driven workforce analytics. They apply to vendors like us, not only to employers. Five positions matter:")
table(["Topic", "What the guidelines now say", "Ref."], [
    ["Tracking productivity", "“Legitimate interest” – the legal basis our DPAs use – is generally **not** valid for continuous or daily collection of individual productivity data (app usage, meetings, email volume). Employers need a stronger basis: a works-council / collective agreement, specific national employment law, or genuinely free consent. Vendors whose standard DPA pre-selects legitimate interest may themselves be liable and should tell clients when guidance changes.", "Para. 34"],
    ["Employee consent", "Consent at work is presumed **not** freely given unless the company proves all four of: (a) no penalty or loss of access for saying no; (b) separate choices for separate purposes – no single “I Agree”; (c) a real alternative way to do the task; (d) withdrawal as easy as giving consent. Acceptance rates above 90–95% are a red flag.", "Para. 47"],
    ["Predictive scores", "Sentiment, burnout and flight-risk scores about individual employees are “profiling”. The automated decision-making protections (Art. 22) apply **when the per-employee score is created and stored**, even if clients only see aggregated team reports. Required: meaningful explanation of the logic, a way to get human review and contest a score, and bias/accuracy testing. Regulators prefer designs that never create individual scores.", "Para. 58"],
    ["Training our AI models", "Using client data to train our own models is a **separate purpose** needing its own legal basis, its own description in DPAs and privacy notices, and its own retention rule. Pseudonymised data is still personal data. A vendor training its own product models may be a **controller** (not just a processor) for that activity.", "Para. 71"],
    ["Sending data to the US for training", "A general Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) does not cover model-training transfers; a standalone, model-training-specific TIA is required. The SCC contract “module” must match the parties’ real roles for each purpose; the wrong module makes the SCCs ineffective.", "Para. 83"],
], widths=[1.2, 4.8, 0.7], font=8.5)

doc.add_heading("2.2 The Dutch AP’s TalentScope fine (Decision AP-2025-0042, published 15 January 2025)", level=2)
para("TalentScope B.V. is an Amsterdam-based workforce analytics SaaS vendor acting as processor for employer clients – the same model as PulseView. The investigation began in April 2024 after complaints from **works councils** at two Dutch clients. The AP fined TalentScope **€8.5 million (about 2.8% of its €303.6 million worldwide turnover)** for four violations, assessed together:")
table(["#", "Violation found", "Key point for us"], [
    ["1", "Wrong legal basis – legitimate interest for continuous productivity tracking (Art. 6(1))", "The processor was held responsible because its own DPA template and system design built in the invalid basis. It could not hide behind its clients."],
    ["2", "No DPIA specifically covering predictive scoring (Art. 35)", "A general platform DPIA was not enough; each high-risk feature needs its own analysis, including per-employee scoring and Art. 22."],
    ["3", "Raw survey and productivity data kept for 30 months (Art. 5(1)(e))", "The AP said 12 months is enough for analytics; “more data improves analytics” is no justification; model training cannot justify retention without its own legal basis. Truly anonymised reports may be kept indefinitely."],
    ["4", "No purpose-specific TIA for US model-training transfers (Art. 46(1))", "Pseudonymisation alone did not cure it; the general TIA was ~18 months old and never reviewed. The AP also flagged that the SCC module should match the parties’ real roles."],
], widths=[0.3, 2.6, 3.8], font=8.5)
para("**Aggravating factors:** several hundred thousand employees affected; violations still unremedied at decision date; earlier works-council warnings ignored; vulnerable data subjects. **Mitigating factors:** cooperation; pseudonymisation and minimum cohort sizes; no proven individual harm. **Lesson:** speed of remediation and responsiveness to warnings directly affect the size of a fine. TalentScope may appeal; that would not change the guidance or the AP’s stated approach. The AP also signalled it will pursue US-headquartered groups through their EU subsidiaries.")

content.text:
I wrote and validated the executive regulatory brief for NovaBridge leadership on EDPB Guidelines 03/2024 and the Dutch AP's €8.5M fine against TalentScope (AP-2025-0042). It shows PulseView matches all four grounds of that fine and that the consent flow fails all four parts of the new consent test. It sets out a new rating for each tracker item where the tracker still says Green, plus a remediation plan for before the Q3 2025 IPO and the decisions leadership needs to make.
It also corrects errors in the source documents. The legal maximum fine is €20M, not the €11.576M shown in counsel's memos and the tracker. Our 24-month productivity-data retention is shorter than TalentScope's 30 months, not longer. And it flags a TIA dated March 2023 that cites the Data Privacy Framework decision from July 2023, plus inconsistent dates across documents.
